content:
The "transition generation" typically refers to individuals born between 1943 and 1960 (or a similar range depending on the context, often related to pension or retirement age adjustments). This group may experience transitional rules in pension calculations.

Regarding the AHV pension (Alters- und Hinterlassenenversicherung, the Swiss Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance), early payment of the pension generally **reduces the monthly amount**. In Switzerland, if you claim your AHV pension before the full retirement age, the monthly pension is lower compared to claiming it at or after the full retirement age. The reduction is proportional to how many months early you claim the pension. Conversely, delaying the payment increases the monthly pension amount.
